ken_build: CI 'publish-image' red on master — docker push failed with 401 Unauthorized. This started right after I changed Dockerfile to add a symlink + chown in the final stage.

maria_infra: ugh, 401 usually auth. can you paste the push stderr?

ken_build: here is the tail: `denied: access forbidden` then `error: failed to push some refs`. exact snippet:
```
The push refers to repository 'registry.internal/redwood/app'
unauthorized: authentication required
```

alex_dev: did the registry rotate creds? or did CI token expire? CI job that does push uses a short-lived token fetched at job start.

ci-bot: [build-4578] fetched ephemeral registry token (issued_at=2024-07-26T14:02:10Z, ttl=10m)

ken_build: hmm the job start time was 14:01:40Z — token should be valid. But I did a multi-stage build that takes ~9m now because of added rsync step and chown, so token might have expired by push time.

maria_infra: that timing makes sense. we saw similar flakes where builds run long and TTL insufficient. but also can be credential helper cache returning stale creds when we do `docker login` inside job. which builder are you using? buildkit or kaniko?

ken_build: using buildx (buildkit). No explicit `docker login` step — we rely on the CI agent to provide `DOCKER_AUTH_TOKEN` to buildx via `--creds` plugin.

alex_dev: could also be cache corruption: if the layer content changed because of symlink ordering, the manifest might mismatch and the registry rejects a push attempt that looks replayed. What do the registry logs show? ops_bot, any logs?

ops_bot: registry logs for that push attempt: `401 token invalid` for subject ci-agent-42, token id expired. No digest mismatch entries around the time.

maria_infra: ok two likely causes: token TTL too short for extended build or CI agent not refreshing login before push. quick triage steps: 1) rerun job to confirm transient, 2) if repro, try forcing a login just before push: `docker logout registry.internal && docker login -u _token -p $REFRESHED_TOKEN registry.internal` 3) increase token TTL or refresh token in CI pipeline.

ken_build: reran the job with manual restart -> same failure on second run. I then added a `sleep 1` between final layer and push to check timing (lol) and captured env: `CI_TOKEN_EXP=0` — weird.

alex_dev: can you reproduce locally with same buildx args? maybe `buildx build --push --progress=plain` to see which step takes longest.

ken_build: repro locally -> build finishes fast (2m), push succeeds. On CI the build takes ~11m. I instrumented the job and saw `kaniko-cache: hit` step slows on first pull of base image layers (network flake). That pushed the push past token TTL.

maria_infra: root cause: token TTL too aggressive for our slowest build path. short-term fix: add explicit token refresh before push step and make the CI job do a `docker login` with a fresh token. Longer term: extend TTL for CI-issued tokens for the publish pipeline or add automatic refresh hook in build step.

ken_build: implemented quickfix: inserted `./ci/refresh_registry_token.sh` just before push which calls auth service and sets DOCKER_AUTH_TOKEN. reran -> push passed.

alex_dev: can you paste the refresh script? we should standardize in other pipelines.

ken_build: script (simplified):
```
#!/bin/bash
NEW=$(curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $CI_SERVICE_TOKEN" https://auth.internal/redwood/token?scope=push)
export DOCKER_AUTH_TOKEN="$NEW"
printf "%s" "$NEW" | docker login registry.internal --username _token --password-stdin
```

maria_infra: nice. create a follow-up to add this as a reusable step in `ci-templates` and increase default TTL for publish tokens. also add a metric in console to alert when push fails with 401 > 3x in 1h.

ken_build: filing ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-1876 (adds refresh step + TTL bump). tagging @oncall infra.

alex_dev: moving forward, also be careful with the Dockerfile symlink/chown: it changed tar ordering which made build slower and larger, might have impacted cache hit rate. consider reordering to avoid touching large directories during chown.

ken_build: ack. will refactor to `COPY --chown=app:app` earlier and remove explicit chown where possible. thanks for the quick help :thumbsup:

maria_infra: sweet. I'll roll the TTL change Monday and add the reusable step. leaving this thread open until INFRA-1876 is closed. :eyes:
